title: Two sides of every contemplation: the bina that grasps and the chachma that wonders
overview:
Chapter four said that contemplation must go into every particular, and this book promises to explain them all. Before it does, chapter five explains how such contemplation is done without fooling oneself. Every contemplation of how something comes from nothing has two sides. The *bina* side, the "hearing", grasps fully how the *yesh* comes out of the *ayin*, and it brings joy: he feels himself getting bigger. The *chachma* side, the "sight", sees in a flash that what brings it into being is beyond all grasp, and it brings *bittul*: the more he delves, the farther away it gets, like a giant who keeps growing. The example is the orbits, the whole gigantic universe, which come from a glimmer of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*; and the same holds in *Atzilus*.

The great principle is that the two come together, in exact proportion. Whoever has the understanding without the *bittul* understood nothing, and whoever claims *bittul* without the understanding is having dreams, and is no humble man at all. Rabbi Markel takes this on to the two camps he sees around him: the *ovdim* who will not study and the *maskilim* who only collect points.

sections.title: Every particular must be known: a promise, and first a warning about how
sections.summary: Contemplating in particulars needs every level of the worlds, which no other book makes available; this book promises to explain all of it. But first it must explain how to contemplate without fooling oneself.

phrases.he: (ה) והנה אחר שנתבאר שצריך להתבונן דרך פרט דוקא,
phrases.en: (5) Now, after it has been explained that one must contemplate *derech prat* (in particulars), *davka*,

phrases.he: הרי מן ההכרח לידע כל פרטי חילוקי המדריגות
phrases.en: it is necessary to know all the particular differences between the levels

phrases.he: בכל פרטי סדרי ההשתלשלות דאבי''ע, להתבונן בהם
phrases.en: in all the particular orders of the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chain of descending worlds) of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, to contemplate them,

phrases.he: אשר אינם מובנים לכל מכללי התורות כו'
phrases.en: which are not understood by everyone from the general body of the teachings.

blocks.text: "Chapter five is a very important chapter." It explains what a thing is from the side of *chachma* (wisdom, the first flash of an idea) and what it is from the side of *bina* (understanding), and how the two work together when one studies *Chassidus*. It really belongs as well with the chapters from about 25 onwards, on the unity of the service.

We said that one has to contemplate each particular thing and know all the different details: so that is what one has to know.

And this, he is telling you, is not available anywhere else. **The general body of the teachings** means something like *Etz Chaim*. Certainly not from the *Zohar* or the *Sefer Yetzira*; and even from the works of the *Arizal* it is not easy, it is not possible, to understand what they are talking about. So what is the solution?

phrases.he: ויבוארו כולם בקונטרס מיוחד,
phrases.en: They will all be explained in a special tract,

phrases.he: מן הצריך מכל פרט,
phrases.en: what is needed from every particular,

phrases.he: וממילא יובן למבין ויודע כמה פרטים אחרים
phrases.en: and from them, one who understands and knows will automatically understand many other particulars.

blocks.title: Shaking the Megillah
blocks.text: **They will all be explained in a special tract.** Here you have to do what you do with the Megillah. "You know what I'm talking about?" "No, I don't." When you read the Megillah and say "this second letter", you shake the Megillah, to show that this is the letter they are talking about. So when you say **a special tract**, you have to shake this book, to show that this is the book we are talking about.

What he gives you here is a promise that he is going to explain everything; everything is explained in this book. "What do you mean? It's not totally everything." He says: "What I'm explaining to you is **what is needed from every particular**, and when you understand it well, you'll automatically understand all the particulars, everything."

That is a very big promise. He is basically telling you that he is going to explain the whole of Kabbalah and *Chassidus* in this book, with all the particulars: everything you need to be able to do what he said in chapter four.

phrases.he: אך תחילה צריך להקדים באיכות ההתבוננות
phrases.en: But first one must explain the how of the *hisbonenus* (contemplation),

phrases.he: גם בדרך פרט,
phrases.en: even in the particular way:

phrases.he: עוד ענין אחד הצריך ביותר
phrases.en: one more matter, which is most needed

phrases.he: לכל החפץ באמת בקרבת אלהי״ם
phrases.en: by everyone who truly wants closeness to G-d

phrases.he: ואינו רוצה לצאת ידי חובתו
phrases.en: and does not want just to discharge his duty

phrases.he: להטעות את עצמו כו'
phrases.en: and fool himself.

blocks.text: **But first**: before we get to the particulars, which start in chapter seven and go through the end of the book. He told us what the *hisbonenus* is, what it is about, the *seder hishtalshelus*, and that it has to be done in the particular way. Now he is going to explain the how of it: there is a certain way it has to be done, if you want to study properly and not fool yourself, or just be *yotzei*: "Oh yeah, I learned a *sicha* today."

sections.title: The something, which lies well in the mind, and the nothing, seen in a flash
sections.summary: Every contemplation has two sides: how the *yesh* comes from the *ayin*, which can be explained until it lies well in the brain, and the infinite *ayin* itself, which no explanation reaches but which flashes in the mind. That flash, like seeing an airplane fly, is more certain than any explanation.

phrases.he: והוא בהיותו ידוע שבכל התבוננות בענין אלה״י דהתהוות יש מאין
phrases.en: It is this: it is known that every contemplation of a G-dly matter, of how something comes into being from nothing,

phrases.he: בכל מקום לפי מה שהוא,
phrases.en: wherever it is, according to what it is,

phrases.he: הרי כולל ב' ענינים
phrases.en: includes two things.

phrases.he: הא' בחינת ביטול היש לאין,
phrases.en: The first is the *bittul* (nullification) of the *yesh* (something) to the *ayin* (nothing),

phrases.he: שזהו השגת ערך הבעל גבול תחילה באיכות אופן התהוות מציאותו מאין כו'
phrases.en: which is the grasp of the relation of the limited thing, first of all of how its existence comes into being from nothing;

blocks.text: Any kind of *hisbonenus* at all, wherever you learn *Chassidus*, no matter what it is, **includes two things**. The first is the *bittul* of the *yesh* to the *ayin*: how the something comes out of the nothing.

phrases.he: שזה קרוב אל השכל ביותר
phrases.en: and this is very close to the intellect,

phrases.he: על ידי כמה מיני הסברים ודמיונות המשלים, וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: through all kinds of explanations and images, *meshalim* (analogies), and the like,

phrases.he: עד שנתאמת במוח היטב
phrases.en: until it becomes well established in the mind

phrases.he: (בל"א עש לייגט זיך אין מוח זייער כו')
phrases.en: (in Yiddish: it lies very well in the brain).

blocks.text: How the something comes out of the nothing can be understood with a total understanding, through all the explanations, images and *meshalim*. In Yiddish, *es leigt zich in moach zeier*: "it lies real good in the brain." This is something that can be explained until it *mamash* lies well in your brain.

phrases.he: והב' ענין בחינת האין האלה״י המהווה אותו
phrases.en: The second is the G-dly *ayin* that brings it into being,

phrases.he: ואיך שהוא נבדל בערך,
phrases.en: and how it is separate beyond relation,

phrases.he: להיותו בלתי בעל גבול כו'
phrases.en: being without limit.

phrases.he: וזהו הנעלם מעיני השכל בהשגה גמורה
phrases.en: And this is hidden from the eyes of the intellect, from a total *hasaga* (comprehension),

blocks.text: The other thing: when you learn how something comes into being, there is also where it is coming into being from, the G-dly *ayin*, which is totally infinite. And infinite does not even mean what most people think, like an infinite number or something like that. It means totally infinite: totally undefined. **This is hidden from the eyes of the intellect**: it cannot really be understood in a total *hasaga*.

phrases.he: רק מכל מקום יוברק כמו ברק
phrases.en: only, all the same, there flashes like lightning,

phrases.he: בסקירה בעלמא במוחו
phrases.en: in a mere glance, in his mind,

phrases.he: אמיתת ענינו כמו שהוא
phrases.en: the truth of what it is, as it is,

blocks.text: Remember: a flash is a matter of *chachma*. The first side, the total *hasaga*, is a matter of *bina*; and at the same time there should be a flash of what it is really talking about. The explanation cannot really tell you what it is, but there should be a flash of *chachma* into what it really is, **as it is**.

phrases.he: אבל הוא בבחינת ההעלם
phrases.en: but it is in a way of *helem* (concealment),

phrases.he: כאילו נתאמת הדבר בראיה חושיית
phrases.en: as if the thing had become real to him by physical seeing.

blocks.text: **But it is in a way of *helem***, and yet **as if the thing had become real to him by physical seeing**. A mental seeing is like a physical seeing.

blocks.title: Explaining an airplane, and seeing one fly
blocks.text:
Take an airplane. To somebody who never heard of an airplane, you could explain the whole business of aerodynamics and the mathematics of it, until he understands that this thing could work. Like the Wright brothers: there never was an airplane, and yet they figured, "Hey, according to aerodynamics, and look, birds can fly, so we can make an airplane work."

Then there is somebody you didn't explain nothing to, but he saw an airplane fly. A guy like that you couldn't even convince that there can't be such a thing. "What do you mean there's no such thing as an airplane? I saw it." The one who has all the explanations, I can give him better explanations that it's not possible, and convince him. But somebody who saw an airplane fly, there is no way to convince him out of it.

So this flash, even though it is in a way of *helem*, is not really an explanation, and he does not really know the *pratim* (particulars), is in a way a stronger conviction than the explanation. The same as with the airplane: the guy who saw it, there is no way you can convince him that there is no such thing.

sections.title: The sight of chachma brings bittul, the hearing of bina brings joy
sections.summary: The flash of *chachma* is a seeing with the mind's eye; its response is *bittul*, not feeling himself and not even feeling that. The full grasp of *bina*, the hearing, brings felt joy: the more he grasps, the bigger he feels. And they run opposite: the more he delves, the more *bina* grasps and the farther away the *ayin* gets.

phrases.he: והוא ההפרש
phrases.en: And this is the difference

phrases.he: בין בחינת ראיה דחכמה כח מ''ה שבנפש,
phrases.en: between the *re'iya* (sight) of *chachma*, the power of *mah* in the soul,

phrases.he: שרואה ולא בראיה חושיית כי אם ראיה שכליית
phrases.en: which sees, not with physical sight but with the sight of the mind,

phrases.he: בהברקה למעלה מן השגה הגמורה
phrases.en: in a flash, above complete comprehension,

blocks.text: **The sight of the mind**: he sees with his mind's eye. **In a flash, above complete comprehension**: he sees a flash of the thing, not by chopping it up in an explanation.

phrases.he: ועל כן ההתפעלות מזה אינו רק בחינת הביטול
phrases.en: and so the *hispaalus* (emotional response) from it is only *bittul*,

phrases.he: שהוא רק העדר הרגשת עצמו מכל וכל כו'
phrases.en: which is only the absence of feeling himself, altogether

phrases.he: (בל"א ער ווערט צו רירט פון ארט
phrases.en: (in Yiddish: he is moved from his place,

phrases.he: ואינו מרגיש גם זה גופא כו')
phrases.en: and does not feel even this itself),

blocks.text:
The *hispaalus* that comes from the *chachma* is a nullification to the idea: basically, the lack of feeling of himself. In Yiddish, *er vert tzerirt fun ort*: he is totally removed from feeling, **and does not feel even this itself**. He does not even feel that he is not feeling it. Why? Because when he has the flash, all he feels is the flash; he does not feel himself, and he does not even realize that he does not feel himself. That is the sign of the flash of *chachma*.

That is the first half of the difference the text began a few lines back, "between the sight of *chachma*", and now it goes on:

phrases.he: ובין בחינת שמיעה דבינה,
phrases.en: and the *shemiya* (hearing) of *bina*,

phrases.he: שבאה בהשגה גמורה ממש,
phrases.en: which comes in a complete *hasaga*, *mamash*,

phrases.he: שהוא באיכות התהוות היש מאין כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: in how the something comes into being from nothing, as said above;

blocks.text: **A complete *hasaga*, *mamash***: the mind goes into the *meshalim* and into the stuff, *mamash*. You know what *hasaga* means? It is from *masig gvul*. You know what a *masig gvul* is? He moves the fence into the other guy's property: he actually goes into the other guy's property. That is what *hasaga* means, that your mind actually goes into the actual domain of the thing.

**In how the something comes into being from nothing**: as in the various ideas of how the worlds of *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* come out of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, and also the matter of the *yichuda ila'a* (the higher unity).

phrases.he: שההתפעלות מזה הוא השמחה במורגש וטוב לב
phrases.en: and the *hispaalus* from this is *simcha* (joy), felt, and a good heart.

phrases.he: כל שמשיג יותר, יותר טוב לו,
phrases.en: The more he grasps, the better it is for him

phrases.he: (בל"א עש איז זייער גוט ומחי' לנפש כו')
phrases.en: (in Yiddish: it is very good, and gives life to the soul),

phrases.he: וכל שמעמיק יותר, יותר משיג
phrases.en: and the more he delves, the more he grasps.

blocks.text: Here the *hispaalus* is exactly the opposite. It is not that he does not feel himself; just the opposite, he feels himself more and more. **The more he grasps, the better it is for him**: the more he understands, the happier he is.

In Yiddish, *es iz zeier gut*: a real good thing, and a real *mechaye* for him, *mamash* a *mechaye*. "Wow, I'm getting such big *hasagos*, and I'm *mamash* growing and growing with this thing." He feels that he is getting bigger. He actually feels it: it is a good thing for him, and he is getting bigger. **And the more he delves, the more he grasps**: the deeper he looks into it, the more he understands, the more he *chapt*.

phrases.he: ובבחינת הראיה דחכמה הוא להיפוך,
phrases.en: And with the *re'iya* of *chachma* it is the opposite:

phrases.he: כל שיעמיק יותר, יותר יפלא ממנו
phrases.en: the more he delves, the farther beyond him is

phrases.he: מהות בחינת האין האלה״י המהווה כו'
phrases.en: the *mahus* (what it is) of the G-dly *ayin* that brings into being,

blocks.text: **With the *re'iya* of *chachma* it is the opposite**: the more he looks into it, the farther away it is.

blocks.title: The Aibershter on the second floor
blocks.text:
Somebody who doesn't know *Chassidus* at all says "the *Aibershter*" (G-d), and he thinks that we live on the first floor and the *Aibershter* lives on the second floor. Somebody who learns a little bit more says the *Aibershter* lives on the tenth floor. Then it becomes the Empire State Building. Then, "Oh no, it's in the clouds." Then, "No, it's all the way up to the moon." Each time it goes farther and farther away.

Somebody who didn't learn *Chassidus* almost thinks the *Aibershter* is almost a physical thing. A spiritual physical thing, you know, made out of air or something: we are made out of lead and the *Aibershter* is made out of helium. It's almost like that. Whereas the more you learn *Chassidus*, the more you see that it is totally, totally beyond.

And this thing that is totally beyond is even *Malchus* of *Asiya*, never mind the higher levels. The more he delves, the farther beyond him is **the *mahus***: what it actually is, not the *metzius*. *Metzius* is knowing what the various relationships are; but what it really is goes farther and farther away.

phrases.he: בהפלאת הערך יותר ויותר כו'
phrases.en: in *hafla'a* (wonder) beyond relation, more and more,

phrases.he: עד שיצטער וידאג כו'
phrases.en: until he grieves and worries

phrases.he: (כמ"ש בכתבי'12)
phrases.en: (as is explained in the writings).

blocks.text: **Until he grieves and worries**: till it *mamash* makes him sad, and he worries that it is going farther and farther away. "How will I ever understand this at all? How will I have a connection to this?" As is explained in the writings.

sections.title: Two opposites at once: a worried heart and joy
sections.summary: Whoever learns in particulars properly gets both at the same time: worry at how far beyond him the *ayin* is, which is where true humility comes from, and joy at what he has grasped. The humility is not "I'm not so great as Einstein", but the man who has seen Og and is shown a ten-foot giant.

phrases.he: ולפי"ז הרי בכל מעיין בדרך פרט
phrases.en: So according to this, anyone who looks into it in the particular way

phrases.he: יבוא לכלל ב' ענינים האלה בהתבוננות,
phrases.en: will come to these two things in contemplation,

phrases.he: בהעלם וגילוי
phrases.en: in *helem* and *gilui* (revelation),

phrases.he: והתפעלות הנולד ב' הפכים הם,
phrases.en: and the *hispaalus* that is born: they are two opposites:

phrases.he: לבו דואג בקרבו
phrases.en: his heart worries within him

phrases.he: על עוצם הפלאת ההשגה באין האלה״י המהווה כו',
phrases.en: over how utterly beyond grasp is the G-dly *ayin* that brings into being,

phrases.he: והשמחה מהשגתו בכי טוב באיכות התהוות המתהווה כו'
phrases.en: and joy from his grasp, in a good way, of how what comes into being comes into being.

blocks.text: Anybody who learns properly, in the particular way explained in chapter four, will come to both: the *helem* of the *ayin* that brings into being and the *gilui* of the *yesh* that comes into being. And the *hispaalus* he should get out of it is **two opposites**.

**His heart worries within him** over how utterly beyond grasp the *ayin* is. That gives him a feeling of nothingness: he is a total nothing. And this is where true humility comes from, not from *mussar*-ing yourself out. The real, true humility is not that you think, "Oh, I am not so great as Einstein." That is not such a true humility. That is like saying, "Well, I'm not so tall as Magic Johnson." There is still some kind of a relation.

blocks.title: The circus giant, after Og
blocks.text:
A guy saw Og, king of Bashan. They tell him, "Hey, we're going to the circus to see a giant," and at the circus they show him a guy ten feet tall. "Here, look at the giant." "Is that a giant?" He is used to Og, who can lift up a mountain, a giant a thousand feet tall or something. *Moshe Rabbeinu* was eighteen feet tall, he jumped eighteen feet in the air, his sword was eighteen feet, that makes fifty-four feet, and he hit Og in the ankle. His ankle was fifty-four feet up. And here they show him a guy ten feet tall: "That's a giant?"

The same here: the more he understands, the more he is *batel* (nullified). The greater the wonder, the bigger the giant gets. Before, he thought it was a ten-foot giant; now he sees, "Wait a minute, if you jump fifty feet in the air, you're just going to hit his ankle." So **his heart worries within him**.

So those are the two things. One, he *mamash* worries about how far this thing is away from him. And at the same time he is very happy from what he understood: **joy from his grasp** of how the something comes out of the nothing.

sections.title: The example from the lowest level: the orbits and Malchus of Malchus of Asiya
sections.summary: The whole gigantic universe, every star an atomic explosion, comes from the outer vessels of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*; grasping that brings joy. What that source is stays hidden: the mind only concludes that it must be so (*muchrach b'hasaga*), and the response is a "wow": I can't even imagine.

phrases.he: כמו על דרך דוגמא
phrases.en: For example:

phrases.he: המתבונן דרך פרט בהתהוות הגלגלים
phrases.en: one who contemplates, in the particular way, how the *galgalim* (the orbits) come into being

phrases.he: מאין האלה״י שהיא מבחינת כלים חיצונים דמלכות דמלכות דעשיה
phrases.en: from the G-dly *ayin*, which is from the outer vessels of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*,

phrases.he: שהוא רק מבחינת כלי חיצוניות, הארה דהארה לבד,
phrases.en: which is only from the outer vessels, a glimmer of a glimmer only,

phrases.he: המאיר בנפש של זה הגלגל בהשגה במהווה אותו
phrases.en: that shines in the soul of this orbit, in its grasp of what brings it into being;

blocks.text: Notice that he is talking about *davka* the lowest things, *mamash* something you can see. You look around and see the sun and the moon and the stars going around the earth, and the earth too is a big ball going around and around. And how this comes out from **the outer vessels of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya***, **a glimmer of a glimmer only**.

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה גם במלאכים דבריאה דאימה מקננא כו'
phrases.en: and in the same way the angels of *Beriya*, where *Ima* (*bina*) nests,

phrases.he: שמשיגים כח האלה״י דמלכות דמלכות דאצילות כו' המהווה אותם
phrases.en: who grasp the G-dly power of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* that brings them into being;

blocks.text: The same with the angels of *Beriya*: they have an understanding in *bina*, which is the sky above them. They have a *hasaga* in the G-dly power of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* that brings them into being.

So he gave you here another thing. Everybody says there is *yichuda ila'a* and *yichuda tata'a* (the lower unity). Really, in the *yichuda tata'a* there is another one: this physical world, how it comes out of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. Then there are *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, which come out of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*; and then *Atzilus*, which comes out of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: הרי זהו המושג בהשגה,
phrases.en: this is what is grasped in actual *hasaga*,

phrases.he: ויתפעל מגדולת הבורא
phrases.en: and he is moved by the greatness of the Creator,

phrases.he: ואיך שהמה בטלים בתמידות,
phrases.en: and how they are *batel* constantly,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב וצבא השמים לך משתחווים, בסיבובם כו'
phrases.en: as it is written, "and the host of heaven bows to You", in their going around.

blocks.text: **This is what is grasped in actual *hasaga***. Look: the whole universe is so big and so gigantic, with these stars, each star like a gigantic atomic explosion; and all the power of the entire universe is like nothing compared to what *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* is.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת האין האלה״י דמלכות דעשיה המהווה,
phrases.en: But the G-dly *ayin* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* that brings into being:

phrases.he: נעלם מהותו מן ההשגה
phrases.en: what it is is hidden from comprehension;

phrases.he: רק שממילא הוא מוכרח בהשגה,
phrases.en: only, of itself, it is *muchrach b'hasaga* (compelled by comprehension),

phrases.he: אחר התאמת אופן הענין של ההתהוות היש כו'
phrases.en: after the way the *yesh* comes into being has become real to him,

blocks.text:
What is *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* really? **What it is is hidden from comprehension.** We understand the relationship of the world to it, the *metzius*; but the actual *mahus* is hidden.

***Muchrach b'hasaga***: it is not that he actually understands what it is. The mind, the logic, dictates that it must be like that.

blocks.title: The sun, a gigantic atomic explosion
blocks.text: Logic dictates: the whole universe is so big and so strong. Just imagine what an explosion is, and what an atomic explosion is; the sun is a gigantic atomic explosion with such amazing amounts of power, and the sun is just a tiny little dot in the whole universe. And the power it takes for all those stars to go around and around: fantastic amounts of power. All of that is coming from *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. So the mind is compelled: what an amazing thing *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* must be! Not that he actually understands what it is. It is just *muchrach b'hasaga*.

**After the way the *yesh* comes into being has become real to him**: after he goes through the explanation and it is verified to him how the *yesh* of the orbits comes into being from *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*; and not even from *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, but really from just the end of its *heichalos* (chambers), from the *shemarim* (waste) of the *Ofanim*. Once he understands that, he says, "Wow, what it must be!" His mind dictates: if this is only the little bit that comes out of it, imagine what it is!

phrases.he: ובבחינת ההעלם לבד הוא מושג,
phrases.en: it is grasped only in a way of *helem*,

phrases.he: ובהפלאת הערך נבדל דוקא
phrases.en: and in wonder, as separate beyond relation, *davka*.

blocks.text: **It is grasped only in a way of *helem***: only as *muchrach b'hasaga*, not that he actually gets it; **and in wonder**, a total amazement. There is the *hispaalus* from understanding the whole thing, the orbits, this goes around this and that goes around that, and so on: that he understands, and from that he gets *simcha*.

But from thinking about what *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* actually is, what he gets is a wow. A wow means an amazement, a *hafla'a*, a *pele*. "Wow, what a *pele*! What it has to be, I can't even imagine." It is not "imagine what it is": the *hispaalus* is "I can't even imagine." It is totally beyond him, totally removed from him. So it is grasped **as separate beyond relation, *davka***: as how separate it is.

sections.title: The same in Atzilus: what the mind sees above comprehension
sections.summary: In *Atzilus* too the relationships of the lights and the *middos* can be understood by images from below, while the true *ayin* that shines on them is seen only by the sight of the mind. If you think you have understood it, you have not: the explanation that does not point you beyond itself was not understood. The sign is a *bittul* beyond all relation, the real humility, which is not lowliness.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בהתבוננות פרטיות באצילות באורות וכלים,
phrases.en: And so it is in particular contemplation of *Atzilus*, of the lights and vessels,

phrases.he: כמו באצילות אור חסד שבמלכות או באצילות אור חסד שבחכמה
phrases.en: like, in *Atzilus*, the light of *chesed* in *Malchus*, or in *Atzilus* the light of *chesed* in *chachma*,

phrases.he: ואיך שנאצל
phrases.en: and how it is emanated:

phrases.he: יושג על דרך דמיון מאור הנאצל למטה בגילוי מהעלם העצמות
phrases.en: it is grasped by an image, from the light emanated below, revealed out of the concealment of the Essence,

blocks.text: He understands the relationships, and **how it is emanated** in *Atzilus*. **It is grasped by an image**: again, it is not that he understands what *Atzilus* really is. He understands the relationships within *Atzilus* according to the *meshalim* down here.

phrases.he: כמו ויאצל מן הרוח דמשה כו'
phrases.en: as in "and He drew of the spirit" of Moshe,

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: and the like.

blocks.title: Moshe's spirit on the elders
blocks.text: It is the same thing as Moshe drawing from his spirit onto the elders: nothing was lost to Moshe. **And the like**: the various other *meshalim*.

phrases.he: ויושג גם כן בענין התהוות מדות דאצילות
phrases.en: And one also grasps how the *middos* (attributes) of *Atzilus* come into being,

phrases.he: גם שהן בחינת מקוריים נבדלים מן השפעה האלהי״ת בנבראים כו'
phrases.en: although they are sources, separate from the G-dly flow into the creatures,

blocks.text: This too can be understood in *hasaga*: how the *middos* of *Atzilus* come into being, even though they are *mekoriyim nivdalim*, sources that are totally different from the actual G-dly flow into *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*. The actual *middos* of *Atzilus* have nothing to do with those worlds. They are their sources, but they are totally separate from them; the whole of *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* comes out only from *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, not even from *Malchus* of *Atzilus*. And this he can understand.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת אין האמיתי המאיר עליהם מאור עצמות המאצילם,
phrases.en: but the true *ayin* that shines on them from the light of the Essence of the One who emanates them

phrases.he: לא יושג אף בדמיון שכל
phrases.en: cannot be grasped even by an image of the mind,

phrases.he: כי אם בהעלם לבד,
phrases.en: only as hidden;

phrases.he: והוא בבחינת ראית השכל שלמעלה מן השגה ותפיסא ממש
phrases.en: and it is in the sight of the mind, which is above comprehension and grasp, *mamash*,

blocks.text: That **cannot be grasped even by an image of the mind**; **only as hidden**, as we said before: it is *muchrach b'hasaga*, you have to say that it must be so. **The sight of the mind** means that the *sechel* sees that there is something higher than the actual understanding.

So in understanding, at any level of *Chassidus*, there are two things. One, you understand the actual explanation of how the *yesh* comes from the *ayin*. The other, at the same time, you see that there is something totally higher than the understanding. And it has to be simultaneous.

If you think you are really getting it, "now this is what the thing is": look in the introduction to *Etz Chaim*, and in many kabbalistic and Chassidic books. What they tell you is that if you think you actually understand, then you don't understand. "What do you mean? I understand. Maybe *Etz Chaim* is not so easy, but look here, especially in this book, we understand." He says: "Yeah, yeah, you understand the explanation, and you understand how the *yesh* comes from the *ayin*. It's not that you should not understand; just the opposite. But at the same time you should understand that there is something beyond the understanding."

If you don't get that, you lost the whole point. Even the stuff you understand you are not understanding properly, because it did not point you to the part beyond the understanding. If you didn't get how fantastically removed from you *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* is, you really didn't understand how the something came out of the nothing.

phrases.he: וכמאמר לית מחשבה תפיסא בך כו',
phrases.en: as the saying goes, "No thought grasps You at all,"

phrases.he: שהוא מחשבה דבינה כו'
phrases.en: which is the thought of *bina*;

phrases.he: דהיינו שזהו היפך ההשגה,
phrases.en: that is, this is the opposite of *hasaga*:

phrases.he: כי כל שמעמיק יותר, יותר מופלא הימנו
phrases.en: for the more he delves, the more amazingly far from him is

phrases.he: עצמיות אור המאציל כו'
phrases.en: the very self of the light of the One who emanates,

blocks.text: **The thought of *bina***: the thought of understanding. The thought of the *hasaga* of the explanations does not grasp the actual *mahus* of the thing at all.

This sight of *chachma* is the exact **opposite of *hasaga***. The more he learns and the more deeply he thinks into it, the more amazingly far from him the thing is: the actual selfness of the light of the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: והסימן לזה הוא הנולד מזה,
phrases.en: and the sign of this is what is born of it:

phrases.he: בחינת הביטול ביותר כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: the greatest *bittul*, as said above.

blocks.title: Og, and Moshe's "Whoa, dude!"
blocks.text: **The sign of this** is a fantastic humility. The actual humility is not that he is humble next to the ten-foot guy. It is when he realizes what a real giant is, like Og king of Bashan: "Wow, there's no way I'm going up against him." Even *Moshe Rabbeinu* went up against him only because the *Aibershter* promised to help him. Moshe was worried. When he saw Og he said, "Wait a minute! Whoa! Whoa, dude! This guy is picking up mountains and throwing them at us! How are we going to fight him?" So it is a matter of total *bittul* and humility.

This is where the real humility comes from, not from what most people think humility is: basically, being humble that you are five feet tall and the other guy is ten feet tall. Here it is totally beyond relation. "Wait a minute, I'm a total nothing, I'm not even an inch tall. I'm like nothing." The whole universe with the suns and everything is nothing, never mind next to the light of the Emanator: next to *Malchus* of *Asiya*. So what do I have to talk about?

From this comes **the greatest *bittul***, and *davka* this is the real humility. What people think humbleness is, is really *shiflus* (lowliness), and you are not supposed to be lowly. They think you should think, "Oh, I'm not such a big shot, I don't understand so good." He says, "No, just the opposite." He is a big shot. He got the *hasaga* of *bina*, and he knows he got it, and he is very happy from it, and he knows it is good for him. But in comparison with the actual *hafla'a*, it makes no difference how big he is: it is still nothing.

sections.title: Joy and bittul come together, in proportion: the great principle
sections.summary: The *bittul* of *chachma* and the joy of *bina* must come together in every contemplation, and each depends on the other: as big a shot as he becomes in understanding, so humble does he become. This is not a by-the-way; it is the central principle of all *Chassidus*.

phrases.he: ונמצא בחינת הביטול והשמחה שמסתעפים ונולדים מחכמה ובינה שבכל פרט,
phrases.en: So the *bittul* and the *simcha* that branch out and are born of the *chachma* and *bina* in every particular

phrases.he: בהכרח שבאים כאחד דוקא
phrases.en: must come together, *davka*,

phrases.he: בכל התבוננות בכל פרט ופרט דווקא
phrases.en: in every contemplation, in each and every particular, *davka*.

blocks.text: **Must come together**: simultaneously. And if they don't come simultaneously, that means you are not studying *Chassidus* properly.

And this is basically what you see with a lot of these kabbalists: there is either one or the other. Either there is the understanding, and they get to be real big shots and think they are really something now. Or else they don't want to understand nothing; they just want some kind of a sense of *hafla'a* and humility. But since there is no *hasaga*, there is no *hafla'a* either, no real *hafla'a*. It is not a real humility. It is a false humility.

sensitivity.reason: Sweeping criticism of "a lot of these kabbalists" as either self-important or falsely humble.
sensitivity.publishable: There are those who have only one or the other. Either there is the understanding, and they think they are really something now. Or else they don't want to understand anything; they just want some kind of a sense of *hafla'a* and humility. But since there is no *hasaga*, there is no real *hafla'a* either. It is not a real humility. It is a false humility.

blocks.text: **In every contemplation, in each and every particular**: any *hisbonenus* that you go through in this whole book goes into both of these things.

phrases.he: והא בהא תליא,
phrases.en: One depends on the other:

phrases.he: ואם לא השמחה ביש מההשגה בטוב,
phrases.en: if there is no joy in the *yesh*, from grasping it well,

phrases.he: לא יבוא להפלאת וריחוק ההשגה באי''ן
phrases.en: he will not come to the wonder and the remoteness from grasp of the *ayin*.

blocks.text: **One depends on the other**: if you don't get one, you don't have the other either. If he doesn't have the understanding in the *yesh*, he doesn't really have the *hafla'a* in the *ayin*.

blocks.question: And what about the one who says, "I just have the hafla'a. I believe in G-d, I'm a humble guy, a simple little guy; I don't need all this understanding"?
blocks.text: "Hey, how could you be a simple little guy? You don't have the understanding: that means you don't have the *hafla'a*, and you're not really a humble guy. You're really a *ba'al ga'ava* (a proud man). You think you're something." "What do you mean? I don't think I'm something." "Yes, you do. Even if it's a little tiny thing that you think you are. Because you don't have the *hasaga* of *bina*, you're a *ba'al ga'ava*."

phrases.he: ולפי ערך השמחה כך ערך הביטול ממש,
phrases.en: And according to the measure of the joy is the measure of the *bittul*, *mamash*;

phrases.he: כי כפי ערך ההשגה במתהווה, כך ערך ההפלאה בהבדל המהווה כו'
phrases.en: for according to the measure of the grasp of what comes into being is the measure of the wonder at how separate is what brings it into being.

blocks.text: And at the same time: according to how happy he is, and what a great big shot he realizes he is becoming, that he is *mamash* becoming a master of *razei d'razin* (the secrets of secrets), literally, that is how much the *bittul* is; that is how humble he will get. Exactly according to his *hasaga* in how the *yesh* comes into being is the measure of the *hafla'a*: how fantastically above us the *Aibershter* is.

phrases.he: וזהו כלל גדול בכל ההתבוננות בפרט ובכלל
phrases.en: And this is a great principle in all contemplation, particular and general.

blocks.text: **This is a great principle.** It is not just something I'm telling you by the way. It is a *klal gadol*, a general principle, like "Love your fellow as yourself: this is a great principle of the Torah." This is the central principle of the whole of *Chassidus*; in terms of *hisbonenus*, it is the great principle, of every contemplation, particular and general.

sections.title: Two dreams: understanding without bittul, bittul without understanding
sections.summary: Whoever thinks he grasps creation and has no *bittul* has grasped nothing; whoever imagines he is *batel* without grasping it has a *dimyon shav*, a false imagination. In the third class this becomes the two sicknesses: those who say "we are *ovdim*, you are *maskilim*", and the big shots who know only points.

phrases.he: (מה שאין כן מי שנדמה לא שתופס היטב ההתהוות
phrases.en: (Whereas one who imagines that he grasps well how things come into being,

phrases.he: ואין לו בחינת ביטול מצד המהווה,
phrases.en: and has no *bittul* from the side of what brings them into being,

phrases.he: לא השיג כלום בוודאי בלי ספק
phrases.en: has grasped nothing, certainly, without a doubt.

blocks.text: If you don't see any *bittul* there, then he didn't understand nothing. And he says it: **certainly, without a doubt**.

phrases.he: ומי שידמה לו בחינת הביטול בעצמו מצד הפלאת ערך המהווה כו'
phrases.en: And one who imagines he has *bittul* himself from the wonder of what brings into being,

phrases.he: ולא השיג בכי טוב לאופן המתהוה כו',
phrases.en: and has not grasped well how things come into being:

phrases.he: דמיון שווא הוא
phrases.en: it is a *dimyon shav* (a false imagination),

phrases.he: ואין לו בחינת ביטול כלל
phrases.en: and he has no *bittul* at all;

phrases.he: כי הא בהא תליא
phrases.en: for one depends on the other,

phrases.he: לפי ערך דווקא
phrases.en: commensurate, *davka*,

phrases.he: מטעם הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: for the reason said above.

blocks.text: Somebody who thinks, "Well, I'm just having *bittul* because I think of the greatness of G-d," and does not know the matters of the *seder hishtalshelus*: **it is a *dimyon shav***, just a false imagination. **He has no *bittul* at all**: he is not a humble guy.

**One depends on the other**, exactly according to the measure. "It's commensurate. Is that what you call it? Commensurate, right?" According to how much you understand in *Chassidus*, that is how humble you are; and according to how *batel* you are, that is how much you understand in *Chassidus*. In direct proportion to each other.

blocks.title: Motel the humble and the sixth aliya
blocks.text: The next class opens with a student who wants to clarify the humility. He tells a story. In a certain *shtibel* there was a man called Motel der Anav, Motel the humble, well known as a very humble person. And he always had the sixth *aliya*. One Shabbos they didn't give him the sixth *aliya*; they gave it to somebody else. After *shul* he threw a whole big tantrum: "How can he give it to this person? You know that I get the sixth *aliya*!" He went on and on and wouldn't stop. Finally they told him, "What's going on here? We thought you're Motel the humble. Where's your *anivus* (humility)?" He said, "I am an *anav*. Next to G-d I'm nothing. But next to this *patz*?"

blocks.text:
"That's not really what I meant." If you feel that you are nothing compared to G-d but something compared to somebody, you are not a real *anav*. In front of the *Aibershter* you are nothing; not just nothing in front of the *Aibershter*: you are *mamash* nothing. If you know the greatness of the *Aibershter*, you know you are *mamash* nothing.

Not only that: it is explained in *Tanya* that whatever happens is really from the *Aibershter*, *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him). It is straight in *Tanya*. If they gave this other guy the sixth *aliya*, whatever the reason it happened, it was the *Aibershter* that gave it to him. Even if somebody curses you out, it is the *Aibershter* cursing you out; if you get upset about it, you are literally getting upset at the *Aibershter*. So it is basically a lack of understanding. But humbleness does not mean weakness: *Moshe Rabbeinu* was also very strong when somebody came up against him. That is a whole different story.

blocks.title: The sixty-fourth brain
blocks.text: You know how the brains open up into thirty-two and thirty-two, sixty-four altogether? It says that a *talmid chacham* should have no more than a sixty-fourth of *ga'ava* (pride); more than that, and he is called coarse. So why a sixty-fourth? You would think: nothing. But this is what it says, "His heart was lifted up in the ways of G-d." This is the sixty-fourth brain. The sixty-fourth brain is the brain of *ga'ava*, total infinite *ga'ava*; and that is the brain which is basically the actual brain of humility, which proves that he is humble.

blocks.title: Let the one who boasts boast
blocks.text:
Why so? Because it says one should not *shvitz* (boast): not the wise man in his wisdom, not the mighty man in his might, not the rich man in his riches. And they explain that a mighty man does not mean like the Terminator. Who is mighty? He who conquers his inclination. Who is rich? He who is happy with his lot. Who is wise? He who learns from every man. So even about that you are not allowed to be a *shvitzer*. No *ga'ava* is allowed.

Then it says, "but in this let the one who boasts boast." He calls him *mamash* a *shvitzer*, and that means the sixty-fourth brain. It doesn't say it's okay to *shvitz*: he says he should *shvitz*! In what? "Understanding and knowing Me": in knowing *Chassidus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 062, before it rereads these lines.

blocks.text: This is basically what chapter five says: if there is not a total megalomania on the one side, there is not the *anivus* on the other side. If he doesn't have the *hasaga* of *bina* and know it, there is nothing. Notice that he says he knows it, he feels it is good, he is happy from it, he knows it is making him bigger, and he is getting a bigger and bigger ego from the side of *bina*. And then he says, "one depends on the other": according to the measure of the joy is the measure of the *bittul*, *mamash*; according to the measure of the *hasaga*, "I know the *seder hishtalshelus*", so much is the *bittul*.

And he goes even further: if there is one without the other, he calls it, what is it, *dimyonos shav*. "It is a *dimyon shav*, and he has no *bittul* at all; for one depends on the other," commensurate.

So these are basically the two sicknesses. *Kuntres HaHispaalus* (the Tract on Ecstasy) describes all kinds of sicknesses, but the two basic ones are *bina* without *chachma*, and *chachma* without *bina*.

So there are two types of people. There are the people who say they are *ovdim* (those who serve G-d) and we are *maskilim* (people of intellect); and that is already the best of them, the most refined. "You know, the real thing is *avoda*, and you're just into *hasagos*." The thing is, if there is no *hasaga* there is no *bittul*, so their *bittul* and their *avoda* is nothing. Not only that: as all the chapters up to here explain, if there is no *hisbonenus* there is no *avoda*. They are not *ovdim* at all.

sensitivity.reason: Dismisses a camp within Chassidus (those who stress avoda over study) as having no avoda and no bittul at all.
sensitivity.publishable: Some say, "The real thing is *avoda* (divine service), and you're just into *hasagos*." The thing is, if there is no *hasaga* there is no *bittul*; and, as all the chapters up to here explain, if there is no *hisbonenus* there is no *avoda*.

blocks.text: And they don't have a *bittul*. Somebody says, "Oh, I'm *batel* to the Rebbe. What do I need to study this stuff for?" So you're not *batel* to the Rebbe, and you're not *batel* to the *Aibershter*. It is all *dimyonos shav*: you are having dreams. "The Rebbe is *Chassidus*." "Yeah, the Rebbe is *Chassidus*." If you don't want to know the *pratim* of *Chassidus*, it means you don't really want to know about the Rebbe.

sensitivity.reason: Mocks those who claim bittul to the Rebbe instead of study as dreamers.
sensitivity.publishable: Someone may say, "I'm *batel* to the Rebbe; what do I need to study this for?" But the Rebbe is *Chassidus*. Not wanting to know the *pratim* of *Chassidus* means not really wanting to know the Rebbe, and without them there is no *bittul* to the Rebbe or to the *Aibershter*.

blocks.text: Here is the actual verse: "Thus says G-d: Let not the wise man boast of his wisdom, let not the mighty man boast of his might, let not the rich man boast of his riches; but in this let the one who boasts boast: understanding and knowing Me, that I am *Havaya*, who does kindness, justice and righteousness in the earth, for in these I delight, says G-d." That's what I wanted: "in these I delight". These are the people I have delight in; no, "in these" means those people.

It goes even further: righteousness and justice are basically also the matter of *halacha*. What would that have to do with it? The *ki* ("that", "for") has four meanings, and here it is a continuation: understand and know Me, that I am *Havaya* all the way up, who does the righteousness and justice in the earth all the way down. And "for in these I delight" is also a continuation: these things down here are what I wanted up there. The *ratzon* (will) in the *Atzmus* (the Essence) spells out all the way down, "the end of the deed is first in thought". It describes the whole *seder hishtalshelus*. To know it, but not just to know the *seder hishtalshelus* in a mechanistic way: to know that it is *mamash* the *Aibershter*, that this is what He wanted.

And notice what he says: "in this let the one who boasts boast." He doesn't say it's okay; he says you should do it. The other things are not okay, and this he says you should do, like a *mitzva*. You are not just advised, "Oh, well, if you want to, it's okay." No: that is what you should do.

So the biggest criticism is: "Eh, what do you need to study this stuff? You need to be *batel* to the Rebbe, you have to have *hiskashrus* (connection to the Rebbe)." The answer to that is: if you don't have the *hasaga* of *bina*, you don't have the *bittul*. You absolutely don't have the *bittul*.

sensitivity.reason: Part of his polemic against a camp within Chassidus that prefers hiskashrus to study.
sensitivity.publishable: One may hear: "What do you need to study this for? You need to be *batel* to the Rebbe, you need *hiskashrus* (connection to the Rebbe)." The answer is that without the *hasaga* of *bina* there is no *bittul*.

blocks.text: On the other side there are the people who say, "Why do you have to study that? Now you have to study *Ayin Beis*." Those are the people who have *bina* without *bittul*. They don't really have a *bittul*; and like he says, not having the *bittul* shows that they don't understand what they are studying, so they don't have the *bina* either. These are basically the guys who are the big shots of *Chassidus*, who know *Chassidus*. These people are *Olam HaNekudim*, the world of points. They only know points, points; they can't put them together. They know fantastic amounts of points. By him it's all points, points.

sensitivity.reason: Ridicules the learned "big shots of Chassidus" as a world of disconnected points.
sensitivity.publishable: There is also the opposite mistake: *bina* without *bittul*. One who has no *bittul* shows that he does not understand what he studies, so he does not have the *bina* either. He knows a great many separate points and cannot put them together; it is like *Olam HaNekudim*, the world of points.

sections.title: Many fool themselves: the higher, the more real; and the face-kvetchers
sections.summary: Many who were raised on *Chassidus* fool themselves about humility. The fourth class takes the two mistakes apart: for those with only *bina*, the higher worlds are abstract, when the higher you go the more real it gets and the greater the *hafla'a*; those with only *bittul* are not sure who is bigger, they or the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: וכידוע לכל טועמי טעם בהתבוננות באמת
phrases.en: as is known to all who have tasted the taste of contemplation in truth

phrases.he: ואינם מטעים את עצמו כלל
phrases.en: and do not fool themselves at all;

phrases.he: וכאשר יובן כל זה לרגילים בדברי חסידות מנעוריהם כו'
phrases.en: and as all this is understood by those used to the words of *Chassidus* from their youth;

phrases.he: ורבים מאד יטעו בעצמם בכל זה
phrases.en: and very many make a mistake in themselves in all this,

phrases.he: בכמה אופנים שונים וכו'):
phrases.en: in many different ways.)

blocks.text: **Very many make a mistake in themselves in all this**: they think they know *Chassidus*, and they think they are humble, **in many different ways**.

Humility is not what they think, *shiflus*. *Moshe Rabbeinu*, it explains, was the most humble person there was, and yet you see in various places he acted like a king; if they didn't listen to him, he got mad. What kind of humility is this? Because he was comparing himself with the *Aibershter*; not that he didn't know his own level. Just the opposite.

What he says here is just the opposite of what they think. If you are not a big shot in *Chassidus*, you are not a simple guy. You can't call yourself an idiot like "the simpleton believes every word", "I'm just a little nothing who just believes in G-d." He says, "No, you're not. You don't know no *Chassidus*, so how can you be a little nothing who just believes in G-d?" Because one depends on the other.

By the way, this also fits with the matters later on: this is basically the *simcha* of *bina* and the *bittul* of *chachma*, and it belongs with the chapters on the *yichud* of *Abba* (*chachma*) and *Ima* (*bina*), which is constant. "Two friends that never leave each other": you can't have one without the other. If you don't have *bina* you don't have *chachma*; if you don't have *chachma* you don't have *bina*. You can't have just the understanding into it, and you can't have just a *bittul* of *chachma*.
Like what these idiots are saying: "Oh, just blank out your mind." And that's *chachma*? No, there can't be *chachma*, cause there ain't no *chachma* without *bina*. One depends on the other.

sensitivity.reason: Calls those who teach emptying the mind (meditation practices) idiots.
sensitivity.publishable: Some say, "Just blank out your mind." Is that *chachma*? There can't be *chachma* that way, because there is no *chachma* without *bina*. One depends on the other.

blocks.title: Ice cream for the Aibershter
blocks.text: The whole thing is that the original *ratzon* of the *Atzmus* is *davka* for the physical. Not for *Atzilus*, not for any of the worlds: *davka* for the Jew putting on *tefillin*, which means a physical ice cream for the *Aibershter*. As a matter of fact, it's not just *tefillin*: the *Aibershter* *mamash* wants to eat an ice cream, and that is why He gave us the laws of *kashrus*, so He'll be able to taste an ice cream. "And make a *bracha* on it." "So what did He have to come up with an ice cream for?" "'Cause He wanted ice cream. He likes ice cream." No: that there should be a physical *taanug* (delight) that you make the *bracha* on.

Not for *Atzilus*, not for any of the worlds: *davka* for the Jew putting on *tefillin*. And it's not just *tefillin*: the *Aibershter* wants a physical delight, and that is why He gave us the laws of *kashrus* and a *bracha* to make: that there should be a physical *taanug* (delight) that you make the *bracha* on.

blocks.title: Chazir and ice cream
blocks.text: If you drink water and you aren't really thirsty, you don't make a *bracha*, because water has no taste: if you drink it to get down an aspirin, no *bracha*. *Hanaa* means a physical pleasure, like eating ice cream; that you do have to make a *bracha* on, because you are giving the *Aibershter* a physical pleasure. He gets a terrible pain out of having to eat a piece of *chazir*, and a great pleasure out of eating the ice cream.

sensitivity.reason: Continues the anthropomorphic humor: G-d gets a terrible pain from eating chazir and great pleasure from eating the ice cream.

What is forbidden, like *chazir*, is against His will; the kosher ice cream with its *bracha* is His great pleasure.

blocks.text: So this is the sickness of the people who have the *bina*, meaning all the particular points, without the *chachma* of seeing what is past it, how it all gets put together, so that you see there is something beyond the whole thing. They say, "What do you mean? We see that there's something beyond this whole thing. Our whole method is that it's all abstract."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: The bachur in the fourth-year class
blocks.text:
"I'll tell you what happened once." A *bachur* came over to Rabbi Markel and told him that *meshalim*, physicalizing the concepts, is only for the first-year class; but he is in the fourth-year class, so that's not for him.

But remember what we learned in chapter four: you start with the orbits and see how it goes up to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, and from this he gets a fantastic sense of *bittul*. By them, actually, there is no sense of *bittul*. Why? Because when you go up to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, by them it is less than what the orbits are.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: What the sun is worth
blocks.text: Take an orbit like the sun. What's the sun? What kind of energy? If you could get the energy of the sun, you could be a zillionaire. What do the Arabs have? The Arabs have energy: that's the whole thing they have, the oil, and the oil is energy. And some of these people are totally bugged out: look how much money this person has. Tell them, "I can give you ten million dollars," and they'll go out of their *keilim*. So the sun is worth more than ten million dollars.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

sensitivity.reason: "The Arabs" as a nation whose whole wealth is oil, beside a remark about people "bugged out" over money.
sensitivity.publishable: Take an orbit like the sun. What's the sun? What kind of energy? If you could get the energy of the sun, you could be a zillionaire. Whole countries are rich from oil, and oil is energy. Tell people, "I can give you ten million dollars," and they'll go out of their *keilim*. So the sun is worth more than ten million dollars.

blocks.title: Buying sunlight at the supermarket
blocks.text: Everything that goes on: the dams they build, you know how much money they get off a dam? Millions of dollars, and that's just from a little bit of sunlight, because the sunlight evaporates the sea water and brings it up the hill. The wind, too: a hurricane caused ten million dollars of damage, and you can harness the wind for money, with electrical windmills. As he explains later in the book, all the *parnasa* (livelihood) we have is from the climate. We were talking about the price of oranges; and not just oranges: everything in the supermarket came from the sun. You are buying transformed sunlight your body can use for energy; that's all you're paying for. And the sunlight that gets to us is just one teeny little ray of the sun out of the whole 360 degrees.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: So this is the *hisbonenus*: look how great the sun is. And the sun is only like a mustard seed in the universe; not even, less than a mustard seed, a tiny speck. Take a mustard seed and put it on your property: what the sun is to even this galaxy is probably less than that. Even the finite numbers we are talking about boggle the human mind; and not the numbers of the molecules, just the number of the stars.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: And all of this comes out from the *Shemarei Ofanim*. It is not even actually coming out: it is induced by them, like a magnet; it is not their actual power.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: And the *Shemarei Ofanim* are just the *shemarim*: their excretion, from their sewer system. And not even the whole sewer system: a speck of their sewer system brings our whole universe into being.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

sensitivity.reason: Renders shemarim, the dregs of the Ofanim, as excretion from their sewer system.
sensitivity.publishable: And the *Shemarei Ofanim* are just the *shemarim*, the dregs; and not even all of them: a speck of their dregs brings our whole universe into being.

blocks.text: And that is only the *heichalos* of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, not even *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* itself, with zillions of angels. You can count the angels in a troop, but "His troops are without number"; and all of that is in one *heichal*, and a troop in a *heichal* is again not even a mustard seed, and the *heichal* is one of many. The *heichalos* are the total externality of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, and that is not even *Malchus* of *Asiya* yet.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: So are we talking about an abstract thing? Not an abstract thing. We are talking about the power of the sun coming from there. It is not abstract.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: The emperor who wanted to see the lion
blocks.text:
Now that we analyze it like that: even an angel. There is a story in the *Gemara*. The emperor, "I don't remember which emperor", saw the verse "A lion roars, who will not fear?" He called the rabbis: "Your Torah is full of nonsense. I'm not scared of a lion's roar. Who's scared of a lion's roar?" They used to have circuses and throw people to the lions, so he'd heard a lion's roar. They told him it is not talking about this kind of lion; it is talking about the upper lion. "I want to see the upper lion. Tell him to come here." "What are you talking about? If he comes here, the whole world will be destroyed." "Either you tell him to come here, or I'll make decrees against the Jews." "Okay, but we warned you."

They told the lion to come, and the lion took one step. Everything shook; an earthquake, things falling down, and the emperor was struck speechless. The lion took another step, closer, and from those two steps almost the whole city was destroyed. "No, no, tell him to go back!" And this is just an angel.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: And he thinks *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is some kind of an abstract thing, an abstract concept. Rabbi Markel told him: no, it is more physical than we are. That doesn't mean it is *gashmi* (material). It means as far as actual energy goes.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49). Rabbi Markel is answering the *bachur* of the story of the fourth-year class.

blocks.title: The atom and the telephone
blocks.text: We know what we are made from. Any scientist will tell you that an atom is an *or* (light) and a *kli* (vessel): there is a bunch of energy, and something that seems to hold it together. And an atomic explosion does not even let the light out of the vessel. It is not the light that is inside the pieces; it is just the energy that holds the atom together, and not even all of it, a tiny bit, the nucleus; and not the power inside the nucleus, just the power holding its pieces together. And that is an amazing power. The telephone I'm holding: if I knew how to take the vessels off, to open up the *kli*, just the power holding its atoms together could blow up the whole universe. So basically we are made from energy.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: Now, when it says *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light), "Oh, it's a *mashal*." What does that mean, a *mashal*? The same as the radiance of the sun, so the radiance of the *Aibershter*, but not an actual light. Or *chachma*: *chachma* does not mean a light, it is like your *chachma* lighting up a concept. Or *chesed*: "the world is built on *chesed*". That is the *mahus*, as against the *metzius* we were talking about, and that is also the matter of chapter five: *bina* understands into the *metzius*, and *chachma* gets the *bittul* from an insight into the *mahus*. That is basically what chapter five is about: the *hasaga* is into the *metzius* of the thing, and the *hafla'a* is into its *mahus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: So what is the *hafla'a*? Wait a minute: look at even *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. You know how many millions of dollars, if you could get *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* to be your *gvir* (rich patron)? You know how much he's got in the bank? What do you mean, in the bank? "Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold." "Oh no, that means *chesed* and *gevura*." No, that means money, man. If the *Aibershter* wanted, right now He could give us a billion dollars.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: A nickel from Bill Gates
blocks.text: And not only that: to say that the *Aibershter* can give us a billion dollars is an insult. It's like saying, you need a nickel, go to Bill Gates, he could give you a nickel. What do you mean Bill Gates could give you a nickel? You'll go to Bill Gates for a nickel? It would *mamash* be an insult to him. "What, are you insulting me? You're taking up my time with nonsense?"
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: They see the hidden world as just some kind of an abstract thing. It is not like that: up there there is more *mahus*, not less. The whole energy of the world, and the whole value, whatever has value here, like gold, and the stock market that works on values: upstairs, as in the first *hisbonenus* we were talking about, from this earth up to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, there is more money.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: More streets up there, and dragons
blocks.text:
And there are more streets. "More what?" "More streets." "Streets?" "Streets, like you live on a street." Where did the street come from? From *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*; and they have more streets up there. Not all the streets came down, the same as not all the light came out of the sun. Up there there are more streets, more houses, more people, more bodies, because all the bodies came from there, and more animals: all kinds of animals up there that we don't even have.

Besides the actual world, all the fantasy worlds have to be up there, like the Star Wars world: any world we have in any fantasy is coming from somewhere. Up there it exists as an actual world: not that it came into existence, but if *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* wanted to, it could make it, with all those creatures. As a matter of fact, all those creatures exist on the next level up from the physical plane, the demon worlds, the world of the imagination, the dream world. In the dream world there are dragons. We don't have dragons; over there they do.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: So they have it totally backwards, totally upside down. Why? Because they don't have the proper *hasaga* into the *meshalim*. The higher you go, the more real it gets, not the opposite. Isn't that the first thing the *Rambam* says: He is the real reality, the real *metzius*, and all *metzius* comes from His *metzius*. He is the real reality, and this world is just a shadow; not even a shadow, a shadow of a shadow. The closer you get to His reality, the more real it is. Not the less real: the more real, and there is more stuff up there. "Yeah, but you're making it physical." No: it does not mean it is physical up there. But it is not that there is less up there; there is more, because the whole of down here is coming from up there.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: When you say *chachma*: "My thoughts are not your thoughts." *Bina* is like *machshava* (thought), *dibur* (speech), *maaseh* (action), and he says, "My thoughts are not your thoughts." When you think something, you can't make it exist. My thought can actually bring a sun into being. So in the thought there has to be more energy than there is in the sun: actual, physical energy. And not only physical energy: such a higher energy that you can't even call it physical anymore, like the whole matter in chapter ten, that it is so high you can't even call it spiritual anymore, or even *chachma*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: So they have it backwards. Why? Because they don't have the *hasaga* of *bina*, so they don't have the sight of *chachma*, and that is why they don't have the *hafla'a*. Why don't they have the *hafla'a*? Because by them, as you go up it gets less: there is nothing up there.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: The Grand Canyon and a herd of elephants
blocks.text: If you learn it properly: you know what a *hafla'a* is? When somebody goes to the Grand Canyon, he gets a *hafla'a*. Or when somebody sees Og king of Bashan: a *hafla'a* and a *bittul*. Or when somebody is standing there and a herd of elephants runs through the town. That is the matter of *hafla'a*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: They don't have *hafla'a* because as they go up they didn't do the proper *hisbonenus*. They didn't make the analysis: if the orbits are so big, and the orbits only come out of the *Sarei Ofanim*, imagine how big the *Sarei Ofanim* are. The *Midrash* basically says it explicitly: as you go up, it is all the more so. More so, not less so; not just some far-off abstract thing up there. That is the thing: the more he delves, the more amazingly far from him it gets. Wow, what can it be already? How much money does this guy have? "Owner of heaven and earth." How much energy can you put up there?
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49), quoting line 38.

blocks.title: Two raging bulls
blocks.text: Who was it that was going to think of the greatness and the power of the *Aibershter*? So he thought of a raging bull running with all this power, knocking things down. "No, that can't be enough for the *Aibershter*." So: two raging bulls. And the people who laugh at this are basically doing exactly the same thing.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: That is what he says, that they have *dimyonos shav*. And then there is the other side: we were just talking about the big *maskilim*; now the guys who have the *bittul* and don't have the *hasagos*. The people who kvetch their faces, the face-kvetchers. Some of these guys, you can *mamash* look inside their brain a little bit and see what they think of themselves: they're not really sure who's bigger, them or the *Aibershter*. Because after all, the *Aibershter* is an *Aibershter*, but they have a *yetzer hara* which they conquered so good. And basically the whole thing is *dimyonos shav*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

sensitivity.reason: Mocks a type within the Chassidic world ("face-kvetchers") as unsure whether they or G-d is bigger.
sensitivity.publishable: That is what he says, that both mistakes are *dimyonos shav*. And there is the other side: those who have the *bittul* and not the *hasagos*. Without the *hasaga*, such a one can come to think a great deal of himself, of how well he has conquered his *yetzer hara*; and the whole thing is *dimyonos shav*.

blocks.title: The satiated lion
blocks.text: Even the way they conquered the *yetzer hara*: what they basically did is feed the *yetzer hara* so good that he doesn't bother them. What they have is a satiated lion. If you have a lion and you keep feeding him a whole bunch of stuff, he'll leave you alone.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

sensitivity.reason: Continues the mockery of the same type: their victory over the yetzer hara is only a fed lion.
sensitivity.publishable: There is a way of conquering the *yetzer hara* that only feeds him so well that he doesn't bother you: a satiated lion. If you keep feeding a lion a whole bunch of stuff, he'll leave you alone.

blocks.title: The Alter Rebbe's beinoni and Yekusiel Liepler
blocks.text:
These people are at least *beinonim*; at least that is how they feel about themselves. If they're making a mistake, actually they're *tzaddikim*; and if they're making a mistake, maybe they're not *tzaddikim*, maybe a *beinoni* who studies all the time. Like Rava, who thought he was a *beinoni*: that kind of *beinoni*. Or a *beinoni* like the *Alter Rebbe*.

The *Alter Rebbe* said, "I'm a *beinoni*." So Yekusiel Liepler told him, "What do you mean? I know that I'm a *beinoni*. If you're a *beinoni*, that would make me a total nothing; and I know I am a *beinoni*, so how could you say that?" The *Alter Rebbe* told him there are different levels of *beinonim*. So they are a *beinoni* at least like the *Alter Rebbe*, not like Yekusiel.
